tools.name: beaconcrm_list_record_types
tools.description: List the record types of this Beacon account (people, organisations, payments, custom types, ...) with their fields (keys, types, options). Call this first: the keys are what the other tools take as `entity` and as field names. GET /entity_types.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_users
tools.description: List the users of the Beacon account (id, role, name, email). Use the inner user.id for 'link to a user' fields. GET /users.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_records
tools.description: List records of one type (for example person, organization, payment), one page at a time. Use beaconcrm_filter_records to search by field values. GET /entities/{entity}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_get_record
tools.description: One record by type and id, with all its fields. GET /entity/{entity}/{id}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_filter_records
tools.description: Search records of one type with Beacon filter conditions (read-only; it uses POST because the filter is a body). Each condition is {"field", "operator", "value"}. Operators by field type: text == != starts_with ends_with contains not_contains null not_null; select (value is an array) contains not_co

tools.name: beaconcrm_create_record
tools.description: WRITE: create ONE new record of the given type in the live Beacon database. Not idempotent: calling it twice creates two records (use beaconcrm_upsert_record to avoid duplicates). Beacon workflows may run as a result. Invalid field values are rejected with the rule that failed. POST /entity/{entity}

tools.name: beaconcrm_update_record
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of ONE existing record. Only the fields you pass are changed; a select or reference field passed as an empty array [] is CLEARED, removing its existing values. The previous values are not kept by this tool. Beacon workflows may run as a result. PATCH /entity/{entity}/{id}.

tools.name: beaconcrm_upsert_record
tools.description: WRITE: create a record, or update the existing one whose key field matches. `primary_field_key` names the field used to find the match (for example "emails" for a person, or "external_id"); `fields` must contain a value for it. If a record matches it is UPDATED with the given fields (an empty array

tools.name: beaconcrm_delete_record
tools.description: WRITE, DESTRUCTIVE: delete ONE record. Beacon keeps deleted records as 'archived' (listable with archived=true), but this server has no restore tool, so treat the deletion as irreversible. Related data that depends on the record may be affected. It is sent once and never retried. DELETE /entity/{ent

tools.name: beaconcrm_trigger_export
tools.description: WRITE: start an export job from an existing export template (created in Beacon). Returns the new export's id with status in_progress; then poll beaconcrm_list_exports with that id until progress is 100 and it carries a download url. Each call starts another job. POST /entity_export/trigger.

tools.name: beaconcrm_list_exports
tools.description: List recent export jobs with status, progress (100 = complete) and, when complete, a signed download url. Pass entity_export_id to check one job started by beaconcrm_trigger_export. GET /entity_exports.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: beaconcrm_list_users, beaconcrm_filter_records, beaconcrm_list_exports · Private data: beaconcrm_list_record_types, beaconcrm_list_records, beaconcrm_get_record, beaconcrm_filter_records, beaconcrm_create_record, beaconcrm_update_record, beaconcrm_upsert_record, beaconcrm_delete_record · Public sink: beaconcrm_list_users, beaconcrm_filter_records, beaconcrm_create_record, beaconcrm_trigger_export · Destructive: beaconcrm_create_record, beaconcrm_update_record, beaconcrm_upsert_record, beaconcrm_delete_record.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: beaconcrm_list_users, beaconcrm_filter_records, beaconcrm_list_exports · Private data: beaconcrm_list_record_types, beaconcrm_list_records, beaconcrm_get_record, beaconcrm_filter_records, beaconcrm_create_record, beaconcrm_update_record, beaconcrm_upsert_record, beaconcrm_delete_record · Public sink: beaconcrm_list_users, beaconcrm_filter_records, beaconcrm_create_record, beaconcrm_trigger_export · Destructive: beaconcrm_create_record, beaconcrm_update_record, beaconcrm_upsert_record, beaconcrm_delete_record

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
